children: Nordic forward power prices fell on Thursday after hitting their highest levels since January 2023 in the previous session, as lower European gas prices and a wet weather outlook weighed on the hydropower-dependent market.
The Nordic front-quarter baseload power contract (NSBLQc1) fell €0.81, or 0.82%, to €98 per megawatt hour (MWh) at 0946 GMT.
Nordic front-year (NSBLYc1) lost €0.35, or 0.58%, to €60.25 MWh.
"Somewhat lower gas prices are pushing down the Nordic contracts a bit today as the weather outlook is almost unchanged," said LSEG power analyst Ole Djupskaas.

Benchmark Dutch and British wholesale gas prices fell as market participants took some profit after contracts rose to their highest since January 2023 and there was no further escalation in U.S.-Iran hostilities reported overnight.
A surge in wind power generation in Germany pushed the country's day-ahead power contract price down.
Nordic water reserves available 15 days ahead (PCAEC00) were seen at 13.47 terawatt hours (TWh) below normal, compared with 13.43 TWh below normal on Wednesday.
"Low pressure activity over northern Europe will continue to dominate the weather in the next two weeks with rather cool and moist air," said LSEG meteorologist Georg Muller.
"The resulting weather will be unsettled across entire Scandinavia and Finland with frequent precipitation and quite cool temperatures," he added.
Germany's year-ahead power TRDEBYc1, Europe's benchmark contract, fell €2.25, or 1.82%, to €121.01 per MWh.
In the European carbon market, the benchmark contract CFI2Zc1 fell €0.43, or 0.51%, to €83.64 a tonne.
